items.text: SEASON 6 · EPISODE 1 · DRAFT · CASE-030  Design studio · Maya, Anselm, Priya and Varga · Level L4 · Intermediate support  Maya’s first week as a junior designer. The courthouse set issues for tender on Monday — and two of her floor boxes are promises nobody else has agreed to keep.  ⚑ RV-140: who signs what. RV-141: figures illustrative. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: The Set
items.stakes: Maya's first week at a drawing board. The set issues Monday, and two of her floor boxes are promises nobody else has agreed to keep.
items.reward: Sheets that agree. Varga's respect. Nothing in the turning space.

objectives.text: Decide what to do with the clash
Find out why the sheets disagree
Look closer: two things about the set

items.rumor: Nothing is wrong with either sheet. They just describe two different buildings.

items.alt: Linden Row Design's studio: tall windows, a pin-up wall of drawing sheets, a long desk. Priya welcomes Maya.

bubbles.text: Four hundred rooms taught you what drawings get wrong. Now you draw them right.

lines.text: A drawing is a promise made on somebody else's behalf. The electrician will build what we draw — if we've told him.
I used to be the one standing on site holding the promise.

items.alt: Friday afternoon. Anselm, the senior designer, gray-haired, holding a marked-up sheet; Maya at her screen with an overlay open.

bubbles.text: The courthouse issues Monday. Check Courtroom 3's floor boxes against electrical before you go.

items.caption: Friday, 3:40 p.m. The set goes out Monday at nine.

items.prompt: Found something? You're looking at that overlay like it owes you money.

options.label: “Two of my boxes sit in the turning space with no conduit. Can I show Varga today, with the numbers?”
options.reply: Today. Engineers like Friday problems better than March ones.

options.label: “It's probably fine — electrical will sort it.”
options.reply: That sentence has paid for a great many change orders.

options.label: “Whose sheet should change?”
options.reply: Ask who owns each line. Then ask them.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #52 · AVERY'S LENS  A drawing is a promise made for other people  Every line you draw commits a trade to build it — check it against everyone else's lines before it leaves the office.  AV-201 promised floor boxes the electrician had no conduit for, in a space the architect had kept clear for wheelchairs.

items.alt: An overlay of AV-201 on the latest electrical sheet: the counsel tables have moved; two red AV floor boxes sit inside the dashed wheelchair turning space with no conduit, clouded in red; the only conduit drawn is a 1 inch run to a power box.
items.caption: Two AV boxes, no conduit, in the one space the building promised to keep clear.

items.title: Background: E-201 rev 2
items.body: Every AV sheet has a small note in the title block: *XREF: E-201 rev 2.* The electrical set is on rev 3. Maya checks the other AV sheets: three more on rev 2. She adds a line to the studio's issue checklist: *backgrounds refreshed today — initials.*

items.prompt: 4:10 p.m. Friday. The set issues Monday at nine. What do you do with the clash?
items.risk: A courtroom built with floor boxes that can't be wired.
timeout: 5:30. The studio empties. The overlay stays open on your screen.
Monday comes with the clash still in the set.

hints.text: Who owns each line — and what would they need to fix it?

options.label: Move the floor boxes on the electrical sheet yourself
options.result: Anselm: “That's Varga's sheet with Varga's stamp. Mark it up; don't edit it.”
options.fail: Never edit a sheet another engineer signs.

options.label: Cloud every clash on the overlay and send it to Varga and Odile today, with the cable list
options.result: Varga replies Saturday morning. Odile explains why the tables moved.
options.consequence: The owners get the evidence while a fix is a line on a drawing.

options.label: Issue as-is with ‘coordinate with electrical’
options.result: The contractor prices boxes with no conduit. A change order arrives in March.
options.consequence: The cheapest place to fix it was Friday.

options.label: Delete the floor boxes and specify wireless mics
options.result: The court's recording needs wired, supervised inputs at counsel.
options.consequence: Deletes a requirement to hide a clash.

items.title: Two buildings.
items.body: AV-201's title block: *background E-201 rev 2.* Electrical is on rev 3, issued twelve days ago after the architect moved the counsel tables to keep a wheelchair turning space clear. Neither sheet is wrong. They describe two different buildings.
items.label: Test: what went wrong — and what catches it?

items.sub: Intermediate · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Anselm and Maya beside a board. Fill is every cable's area added up, over the conduit's inside area, times a hundred. Three or more cables, the usual limit is forty percent. Camera, mic, display link, network: four at fifty square millimetres in a four-ninety conduit… forty-one percent. Over. And it isn't ours to size — we give Varga the numbers; he signs the conduit.

bubbles.text: Fill is every cable's area added up, over the conduit's inside area, times a hundred. Three or more cables, the usual limit is forty percent.

items.caption: Intermediate: the formula and what every letter means. The arithmetic is yours.

items.text: 📗 FIELD NOTES · INTERMEDIATE  Terms   Drawing set   Floor box   Conduit fill   Engineer of record   Formula and variables   ƒ FORMULA · Conduit fill  fill = Σ A cable  ÷ A conduit  × 100   A cable   cross-section area of each cable, mm²  A conduit   internal area of the conduit, mm²  fill  percent of the conduit the cables occupy     ƒ FORMULA · Percentage  % = part ÷ whole × 100   part  the piece you are measuring  whole  everything it is part of

items.label: **Learn it now:** drawings, coordination and conduit fill.

items.title: Blueprints
items.body: In 1842 the astronomer John Herschel invented cyanotype, a way of copying drawings with light-sensitive iron salts. Architects and engineers used it for a century: white lines on blue paper — blueprints. Copies meant every trade could work from the same drawing. It also meant every trade could work from an old one.

items.title: Forty-one percent.
items.body: Even where a conduit is drawn, it's 1 inch. Maya's cable list for one counsel table — two network, two microphone, a display link and control — totals 228 mm². In 557 mm² of conduit that's 41%: over the usual 40% limit. The pull would fight every bend.
items.label: Test: what's the number — and what do you do with it?

items.prompt: Saturday morning. How do you settle the conduit size?
items.risk: A conduit the cables can't be pulled through.
timeout: Monday's set carries the 1 inch conduit.

hints.text: What does the engineer of record need from you?

options.label: Write ‘conduit size by electrical’ and move on
options.result: Varga sizes it by habit: 1 inch.
options.consequence: The designer who knows the cables stayed silent.

options.label: Send Varga the cable list and a fill calculation for each table, and ask him to size it
options.result: Varga: “Forty-one on a run you'll pull again in five years? One and a quarter.” Rev 4 Monday.
options.consequence: Your numbers, his decision and stamp.

options.label: Specify thinner cables so it fits
options.result: The display link loses its distance rating.
options.consequence: Weakens the system to fit a conduit.

options.label: 41 is close enough to 40
options.result: The installer pulls it. A jacket tears in a bend; the link fails in commissioning.
options.consequence: Limits exist for the pull and the heat.

items.label: **Fix it:** plan the fill for Varga — two counsel tables, two conduits.

items.alt: Saturday morning: Maya on a video call with Varga, the electrical engineer of record, gray-bearded, on screen.

bubbles.text: Cable list and fill for both tables. Forty-one in the one inch.
One and a quarter to both. Rev 4 Monday, stamped. Good catch.

items.prompt: Monday, 8:30 a.m. What changes about how the studio issues sets?
items.risk: The same clash on the Playhouse set.
timeout: The set issues. The checklist stays as it was.
The next clash waits for the next Friday.

hints.text: What would have caught this without you?

options.label: Every issue: refresh every background to the latest revision, overlay and cloud clashes, attach fill and load numbers — initialled on the checklist
options.result: Anselm adds it to the checklist himself. Kit grumbles, then finds a clash on the Playhouse set that afternoon.
options.consequence: Coordination becomes a step, not a hope.

options.label: Blame electrical for not sending rev 3
options.result: Varga did send it — to the project inbox nobody read.

options.label: Maya checks every sheet herself every night
options.result: Maya checks forty sheets a night until week three.

options.label: Nothing — it's fixed
options.result: The Playhouse set has the same stale backgrounds.
options.fail: Fix the habit, not only the sheet.

items.text: 📁 CASE FILE · CASE-030 · SIGNAL original  The Missing Conduit  The AV sheet promised two floor boxes. The electrical sheet had never heard of them.   Open the case file ▸   Learn · Service · Engineer — it doesn't change your story progress.

items.alt: The overlay on electrical revision 4: AV floor boxes at the new table positions, clear of the turning space, each fed by a 1¼ inch conduit at 24% fill.
items.caption: Two sheets, one building. Issued at 9:00.

lines.text: Forty-one percent? On a courtroom run you'll pull again in five years? No. One and a quarter.
I'll send you the cable list with it.

items.alt: Anselm and Maya at the pin-up wall; the courthouse sheets stamped ISSUED.

bubbles.text: Twelve days of stale background, caught on a Friday. That's the whole job, you know.
It used to be my Mondays on site.

items.title: Turning space · 1.5 m
items.body: The architect's access review had failed the old layout: no turning space beside counsel. Odile moved the tables 600 mm. The AV boxes followed the old tables — into the one space the building had promised to keep clear.

items.alt: The Wexcombe Playhouse, mid-renovation: the house and the stage; Anselm pointing up at a new steel beam across the ceiling.

bubbles.text: The projector goes nine metres from the screen. The new beam is at nine metres. Who did the throw calculation?

items.caption: Next: *Throw.*

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  Draw on the latest backgrounds, overlay and cloud every clash, and bring the owner the numbers: fill = Σ cable area ÷ conduit area × 100, usually ≤ 40% for three or more cables. The engineer of record sizes and signs.
REFLECTION (optional)  · Maya spent years on site holding other people’s drawings. What would you want the person drawing your next job to check?
